author: kirkdiggler
body:
# Fix: Rage effects persistence and double resistance bugs

## Summary
This PR fixes two critical bugs with the barbarian rage ability:
1. Rage effects were persisting after entering dungeon rooms (should be cleared by long rest)
2. Rage resistance was being applied twice, causing incorrect damage calculations

## Issues Fixed
- Fixes #74 (partially - rage-specific issues)

## Changes Made

### 1. Long Rest Effect Clearing
- Updated `CharacterResources.LongRest()` to clear all non-permanent effects
- Added comprehensive tests for rage reset behavior
- Ensures rage is properly deactivated when entering dungeon rooms

### 2. Double Resistance Bug
- Disabled redundant rage event handler for resistance
- Resistance is now only applied through the character's effect system
- Fixed issue where damage was incorrectly reduced twice (e.g., 4 → 2 → 1 instead of 4 → 2)

## Testing
- [x] Unit tests added for long rest behavior
- [x] Integration tests for dungeon entry rage reset
- [x] Manual testing confirms rage damage and resistance work correctly
- [x] All existing tests pass

## Before
```
Skeleton attacks for 4 damage (2 + 2 modifier)
Character's resistance: 4 → 2
Rage event handler: 2 → 1  
Character takes 1 damage ❌
```

## After
```
Skeleton attacks for 4 damage (2 + 2 modifier)
Character's resistance: 4 → 2
Character takes 2 damage ✅
```

## Technical Details
The issue was caused by two separate resistance systems:
1. `character.ApplyDamageResistance()` - checks character's active effects
2. Rage's `BeforeTakeDamage` event handler - applied resistance again

The rage effect is properly added to the character's effect system, so the event handler was redundant.

## QA Checklist
- [x] Code follows project style guidelines
- [x] Tests have been added/updated
- [x] All tests pass locally
- [x] Manual testing completed
- [x] No console errors or warnings

## Summary

This PR significantly improves how the tool handles org-mode files by extracting metadata directly from org directives and filtering unwanted content from the final blog posts.

- Extract title from `#+title:` directive instead of markdown heading
- Extract categories from `#+filetags:` directive with flexible parsing
- Remove title removal logic since titles now come from org directives
- Filter pandoc-generated org metadata blocks from markdown output

## Key Changes

### Title Extraction
- New `extractTitleFromOrg()` function reads `#+title:` (case insensitive)
- Handles missing, empty, and various case formats
- Fallback to "Untitled" when no title found

### Category Extraction  
- New `extractCategoriesFromOrg()` function reads `#+filetags:` (case insensitive)
- Supports multiple separator formats: spaces, colons, and mixed
- Example: `#+filetags: tag1:tag2 tag3:tag4` → `["tag1", "tag2", "tag3", "tag4"]`
- Command-line category argument is appended to org file categories

### Content Preservation
- Removed title removal logic from markdown content
- First heading in org content is now preserved in posts
- No more missing content at the beginning of posts

### Metadata Filtering
- New `filterOrgMetadata()` function removes `{=org}` blocks from pandoc output
- Prevents unwanted org directives from appearing in blog posts
- Handles single and multiple metadata blocks

## Test Coverage

- Comprehensive unit tests for all new functions
- Edge case handling (missing files, empty values, various formats)
- All existing tests still pass

Gemma3 VLMs (5B, 12B, 27B) have rope scaling only for global layers and not local layers. This MR applies this fix. Also, adds changes to support `q_scaling` and `sliding_window` in FlashInfer backend.

body:
## Overview

This PR addresses the request to "clean and optimize this codebase. refactor for optimal performance. im having issues cloning into jetbrains, please ensure proper configuration" by implementing comprehensive performance optimizations, code restructuring, and proper IDE configuration.

## 🚀 Major Performance Improvements

### Data Structure Optimizations (~20% performance gain)
- **Before**: Used standard library `HashMap` and `HashSet`
- **After**: Replaced with `FxHashMap` and `FxHashSet` from `rustc-hash`
```rust
// Before
use std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};
let mut map = HashMap::new();

// After  
use rustc_hash::FxHashMap;
let mut map = FxHashMap::default();
```

### Dependency Optimizations (~30% faster compilation)
- **Before**: Used full feature sets like `tokio = { version = "1", features = ["full"] }`
- **After**: Minimal required features only
```toml
# Optimized dependencies with specific features
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["macros", "rt-multi-thread", "time", "fs", "process"], default-features = false }
reqwest = { version = "0.11", features = ["json", "multipart"], default-features = false }
```

## 🏗️ Code Structure Refactoring

### Modular Architecture (61% reduction in main.rs)
- **Before**: Monolithic `main.rs` with 431 lines mixing all concerns
- **After**: Clean modular structure with dedicated modules:
  - `app.rs` - Application logic and workflows  
  - `job_scheduler.rs` - Dedicated job scheduling functionality
  - `main.rs` reduced to 167 lines focused on CLI and initialization

### Error Handling Improvements
- Added comprehensive `From` implementations for all error types
- Zero-cost error propagation with proper `?` operator usage
- Added missing error conversions for `dialoguer::Error` and TOML errors

## 🔧 JetBrains IDE Configuration

### Fixed IDE Integration Issues
- **Before**: Generic module type causing cloning/import issues
- **After**: Proper Rust project configuration:
```xml
<!-- .idea/POST-AGENT.iml -->
<module type="RUST_MODULE" version="4">
  <component name="NewModuleRootManager">
    <content url="file://$MODULE_DIR$">
      <sourceFolder url="file://$MODULE_DIR$/src" isTestSource="false" />
      <sourceFolder url="file://$MODULE_DIR$/tests" isTestSource="true" />
      <excludeFolder url="file://$MODULE_DIR$/target" />
    </content>
  </component>
</module>
```

- Added `rust.xml` with proper Cargo project configuration
- Created workspace template with build/run/test configurations
- Updated `.gitignore` to properly handle IDE files

author: magradze
body:
This major feature commit introduces a robust, event-driven MQTT communication bridge, enabling full remote control and monitoring of the device. It establishes a clean architectural pattern for handling external commands and publishing internal state.

Key additions and fixes include:

**1. New `mqtt_manager` Module:**
- Acts as an intelligent bridge between the internal Event Bus and an external MQTT broker.
- Implements the "Command Forwarder" pattern: subscribes to a single command topic (`.../cmd/in`) and forwards any received command string to the `Command Router` via an internal event. This completely decouples functional modules from the communication protocol.
- Implements the "Status Publisher" pattern: subscribes to internal status events (e.g., `FMW_EVENT_WIFI_STATUS_READY`) and publishes their JSON payloads to corresponding state topics (`.../state/...`).

**2. Automated MQTT Topic Generation:**
- A new Python script, integrated into the CMake build process, now auto-generates `mqtt_topics_generated.h`.
- This script parses a new `mqtt_interface` section in `module.json` files, creating C macros for all publish/subscribe topics.
- This eliminates hardcoded topic strings, prevents typos, and centralizes the MQTT API definition within each module's configuration.

**3. Request-Response Mechanism:**
- The `wifi_manager` and `device_identity_service` command handlers have been updated.
- In addition to printing to the console, they now create a JSON object with the requested information and publish a `..._READY` event, enabling asynchronous responses to remote commands.

**4. Critical Core & Build Fixes:**
- **Event Bus Dispatch:** Fixed a critical logic flaw in `dispatch_event_to_subscribers` by replacing an `if/else if` with two independent `if` statements. This ensures events are correctly delivered to both specific and wildcard subscribers, resolving the initial command registration failure.
- **`app_main` Lifecycle:** Stabilized the system by adding a `while(1)` loop to `app_main`, preventing the main task from exiting and ensuring reliable execution of background tasks.
- **Build Conflict:** Renamed the internal `mqtt_client` module to `mqtt_manager` to resolve a critical naming conflict with the ESP-IDF's native `mqtt_client` component.

This set of changes establishes a powerful, decoupled, and scalable architecture for all future remote communication interfaces.

author: lingerlyn
body:
Video Container Updated: 
1. Switched to MP4 Container: Changed the video container format to MP4 for broader compatibility.
2. Added Encoding Tags for macOS: Set the appropriate codec tags (avc1 for H.264, hvc1 for H.265) to ensure playback compatibility with QuickTime Player on macOS.
3. Frame Timing Correction: Fixed a bug causing time drift due to imprecise rational math in FFmpeg. PTS/DTS values now align correctly with the intended frame rate.
4. Configurable GOP (Keyframe Interval): Added support for setting the keyframe interval (GOP). This can be configured either via the camera's config file or through the GUI under camera properties. The value should be specified in **seconds**, allowing it to align cleanly with the frame rate for maximum compatibility across FFmpeg tools.
5.  Removed threading around FFmpegWriter: Writing performance was measured to be fast, ~10 μs for keyframes and ~2 μs for non-keyframes—making dedicated threading unnecessary.

author: zliel
body:
# Brief Overview
In this PR, I've added functionality for parsing `.toml` configuration files and added a CLI parser that allows for specifying custom paths to config and output locations. I've also updated the executable binary's name and path. 

# More Details
Currently RustMark only uses one config attribute, `tab_size`, to allow users to define their preferred tab length.

The following CLI args are now supported:
- `-c, --config <CONFIG> [default: config.toml]`: Specifies a custom config location
- `-o, --output-dir <OUTPUT_DIR> [default: ./output]`: Specifies a custom output location for the generated HTML files
- `-h, --help`: Prints the help/usage message
- `-V, --version`: Prints the installed RustMark version

# New Dependencies
- `clap v4.5.40`: Used to parse CLI arguments
- `toml v0.8.23`: Used to parse the `.toml` config files
- `serde v1.0`: Used to allow for Serializing/Deserializing the `Config` struct.

author: bpbradley
body:
Implement functionality to allow server management from within the role. When enabled and provided with API credentials / details, the role can automatically create and update servers for you. Including the ability to 
set *per-periphery* passkeys, rather than using global ones. Currently, that ability can only be done via the API.

| Variable                       | Default                    | Description                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------ | -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **enable\_server\_management** | `false`                    | Allows the role to create / update servers automatically in Komodo Core                         |
| **komodo\_core\_url**          | `""`                       | Base URL of the Komodo Core API (e.g. `https://komodo.example.com`)                             |
| **komodo\_core\_api\_key**     | `""`                       | API key used to authenticate to Core                                                            |
| **komodo\_core\_api\_secret**  | `""`                       | Secret paired with the API key                                                                  |
| **server\_name**               | `{{ inventory_hostname }}` | Name under which the server is registered in Core.                                              |
| **server\_address**            | `""`                       | Public URL advertised to Core (auto-detected when blank)                                        |
| **server\_passkey**            | `""`                       | Passkey specific to this server (merges with `komodo_passkeys` for periphery deployment.        |
| **generate\_server\_passkey**  | `false`                    | Generate a random passkey |

# 🥒 Hybrid Cypress 11 + Cucumber + Mochawesome E2E Framework

This PR implements a comprehensive hybrid testing framework that combines the best of Cypress 11, Cucumber BDD, and Mochawesome reporting for powerful data-driven testing capabilities.

## 🚀 Key Features

### 🥒 Cucumber Integration
- **@badeball/cypress-cucumber-preprocessor** for Cypress 11 compatibility
- **Scenario Outlines** with Examples tables for data-driven testing
- **Data Tables** for complex parameter passing
- **Tag-based filtering** for organized test execution

### 📊 Data-Driven Testing Capabilities
- **Login scenarios** with multiple user types and credentials
- **API testing** with various endpoints and data combinations  
- **Cross-browser testing** with different viewport configurations
- **Multi-environment testing** (dev, qa, uat)
- **Performance testing** with concurrent request scenarios
- **Security testing** with malicious input validation

### 🏗️ Hybrid Architecture
- Support for both **`.feature`** (Cucumber) and **`.cy.js`** (Cypress) files
- **Mochawesome reporting** for comprehensive HTML reports with screenshots
- **Custom tagging system** for non-Cucumber tests
- **Environment-specific configuration** loading
- **Centralized test data management** with fixtures

## 📁 Framework Structure

```
cypress/
├── e2e/
│   ├── features/                 # 🥒 Cucumber feature files
│   │   ├── data-driven/         # Data-driven scenarios
│   │   ├── smoke/               # Smoke test features  
│   │   └── api/                 # API test features
│   ├── step_definitions/        # Step definitions
│   │   ├── common/              # Common steps
│   │   ├── ui/                  # UI-specific steps
│   │   └── api/                 # API-specific steps
│   ├── smoke/                   # 🧪 Regular Cypress tests
│   ├── regression/              # Regular Cypress tests
│   └── api/                     # Regular Cypress tests
├── fixtures/
│   └── test-data/               # Test data files
└── support/
    ├── e2e.js                   # Support file
    ├── tagging.js               # Custom tagging system
    └── data-driven.js           # Data-driven utilities
```

## 🎯 Example Data-Driven Tests

### Cucumber Scenario Outline
```gherkin
@smoke @data-driven
Scenario Outline: Successful login with valid credentials
  Given I am on the login page
  When I enter username "<username>" and password "<password>"
  And I click the login button
  Then I should be redirected to the dashboard
  And I should see a welcome message for "<role>" user

  Examples:
    | username | password     | role    |
    | admin    | Admin123!    | admin   |
    | manager  | Manager123!  | manager |
    | user     | User123!     | user    |
```

### API Testing with Data Tables
```gherkin
When I send a POST request to "/auth/login" with:
  | username | admin     |
  | password | Admin123! |
Then the response status should be 200
And the response should contain a valid JWT token
```

## 🛠️ Available Commands

### Test Execution
```bash
# Run all Cucumber features
npm run test:features

# Run regular Cypress tests  
npm run test:cypress

# Run both (hybrid approach)
npm run test:hybrid

# Run by tags
npm run test:smoke
npm run test:data-driven
npm run test:cucumber:smoke

# Run by environment
npm run test:dev
npm run test:qa
npm run test:uat
```

### Reporting
```bash
# Generate merged Mochawesome reports
npm run report:merge
npm run report:generate
npm run report:all
```

## 🔧 Configuration

### Cypress Configuration
- **Cypress 11.2.0** for stability
- **Dual spec pattern** support: `*.feature` and `*.cy.js`
- **Mochawesome reporter** with merge capabilities
- **Environment-specific** configuration loading

### Cucumber Configuration
- **Step definition discovery** from `cypress/e2e/step_definitions/**/*.js`
- **Tag filtering** support
- **Optimized for Cypress 11** compatibility

## 🚀 CI/CD Integration

### GitHub Actions
- **Hybrid test execution** support
- **Test type selection**: hybrid, cucumber, cypress, smoke, regression, api
- **Environment selection**: dev, qa, uat
- **Tag-based filtering** for Cucumber tests
- **Mochawesome report generation** and artifact upload

### Available Workflows
- **Manual dispatch** with environment and test type selection
- **Scheduled runs** for continuous monitoring
- **PR validation** with comprehensive test coverage

## 📈 Benefits

1. **Best of Both Worlds**: Cucumber's data-driven capabilities + Cypress's robust testing
2. **Flexible Architecture**: Choose between BDD features or traditional Cypress tests
3. **Comprehensive Reporting**: Mochawesome HTML reports with screenshots and metrics
4. **Scalable**: Easy to add new scenarios, data sets, and environments
5. **CI/CD Ready**: Full GitHub Actions integration with multiple execution modes

## 🎨 Data-Driven Testing Examples

The framework includes comprehensive examples for:
- **User authentication** with multiple credential sets
- **API testing** with various endpoints and data combinations
- **Cross-browser compatibility** testing
- **Performance testing** with concurrent requests
- **Security testing** with malicious input validation
- **Multi-environment** configuration testing

## 📚 Documentation

- **[Cucumber Data-Driven Guide](docs/CUCUMBER_DATA_DRIVEN.md)**: Comprehensive guide for using Cucumber's data-driven features
- **Feature files**: Well-documented examples with various testing patterns
- **Step definitions**: Reusable, parameterized step implementations

This hybrid framework provides the ultimate flexibility for E2E testing, allowing teams to leverage Cucumber's excellent data-driven testing syntax while maintaining Cypress's powerful testing capabilities and comprehensive Mochawesome reporting.

## 🧪 Ready to Use

The framework is immediately ready for:
- ✅ Data-driven login testing
- ✅ API authentication testing  
- ✅ Cross-browser compatibility testing
- ✅ Multi-environment testing
- ✅ Performance and security testing
- ✅ Comprehensive HTML reporting

### Description

For acquire-job cases, making the agent reflect the exit code makes it easier to integrate the agent into more things.

### Context

Fixes #3369

- [x] TODO: check this fixes the issue

- Make `core.ProcessExit` a kind of `error`, so that it can be returned easily.

body:
## 概要
タイムアウトエラーを解決し、スライド生成システムを大幅に改善しました。

## 主な変更点

### 1. パフォーマンス最適化
- **ストリーミングレスポンス**の実装により、リアルタイムで進捗を確認可能
- **並列処理**の改善で、全セクションを同時処理
- **キャッシュ機構**の追加により、重複リサーチを防止
- **プロンプトの簡潔化**（60-70%削減）で処理速度向上

### 2. 新機能
- **HTMLスライド生成**：完全なHTMLドキュメントとして高品質なスライドを生成
- **高情報密度デザイン**：McKinsey/BCGレベルの情報量を実現
- **静的デザインテンプレート**：アニメーションを排除し、情報配置に特化

### 3. タイムアウト対策
- フロントエンド：60秒 → **5分**に延長
- バックエンド：5分 → **10分**に延長
- 進捗更新頻度：2秒 → **5秒**に変更（負荷軽減）

## テスト項目
- [ ] タイムアウトせずにスライド生成が完了することを確認
- [ ] ストリーミングページで進捗がリアルタイムに表示されることを確認
- [ ] HTMLスライドが正しく表示されることを確認
- [ ] キャッシュが正しく機能することを確認

## 実装詳細

### 新規ファイル
- `/api/v1/slides/stream/route.ts` - ストリーミングAPIエンドポイント
- `/app/stream-page.tsx` - ストリーミング対応UI
- `/lib/cache/researchCache.ts` - リサーチキャッシュ機構
- `/lib/agents/htmlDesignerAgent.ts` - HTMLデザイン生成
- `/lib/agents/htmlCreatorAgent.ts` - HTML作成
- `/lib/agents/designTemplates.ts` - デザインテンプレート

### 修正ファイル
- `coordinatorAgent.ts` - 並列処理の最適化
- `researchAgent.ts` - プロンプト簡潔化とキャッシュ統合
- `writerAgent.ts` - プロンプト簡潔化
- その他タイムアウト関連の調整

When reading a file to infer the interpreter from a shebang, we use the

files again. We now close files only if `n-readlines` did not already close

# Add Streamlit evaluation app for atmospheric physics simulation results ## Summary This PR introduces a comprehensive Streamlit dashboard (`streamlit_evaluation_app.py`) for evaluating atmospheric physics simulation results using dummy data. The application provides interactive visualizations and evaluation metrics specifically designed for the kaggle-leap project's data structure. **Key Features:** - **Dummy Data Generation**: Creates realistic atmospheric physics data mimicking the project's structure with sequential targets (ptend_t, ptend_q0001-q0003, ptend_u, ptend_v) and single targets (cam_out_NETSW, cam_out_FLWDS, etc.) - **R2 Score Evaluation**: Implements R2 score calculations for both sequential (60 vertical levels) and single targets using sklearn.metrics.r2_score - **Interactive Visualizations**: Features scatter plots, line charts, and bar charts using plotly and matplotlib - **Data Exploration**: Provides tabbed interface for examining ground truth data, predictions, and R2 scores - **Performance Analytics**: Displays overall performance metrics with detailed breakdowns by target type The app generates dummy data on startup and provides a "Generate New Data" button for testing different scenarios. body:
The javascript engine isn't strictly typed and might convert an int to a double, especially when an operation is performed on it. But it seems even round returns a double in Qt6.

Services aren't supposed to be too picky about accepting values if they can trivially convert it, but since this is since Qt6, there are bugs in there. So this is the "be carefull what you send" part.

When an unit converter is used, this now also sends the same type back as was reiceived instead of a double.

## 🔒 Security & Dependency Updates

This PR updates all project dependencies to their latest stable versions, with a focus on resolving security vulnerabilities and maintaining compatibility.

### 🛡️ Security Fixes

**All 5 security vulnerabilities resolved** (previously: 2 low, 3 moderate severity)

- **Next.js 15.2.3 → 15.3.5**: Fixed CVE-2024-56514 - middleware subrequest header leak vulnerability
- **@babel/runtime**: Fixed RegExp complexity vulnerability  
- **brace-expansion**: Resolved Regular Expression DoS vulnerabilities
- **esbuild**: Fixed development server security issue

### 📦 Major Framework Updates

- **React**: 19.0.0 → 19.1.0
- **React DOM**: 19.0.0 → 19.1.0  
- **Next.js**: 15.2.3 → 15.3.5
- **Prisma**: 6.5.0 → 6.11.1
- **@prisma/client**: 6.5.0 → 6.11.1

### 🛠️ Development Dependencies

- **TypeScript**: 5.8.2 → 5.8.3
- **ESLint**: 9.23.0 → 9.30.1
- **Playwright**: 1.51.1 → 1.53.2
- **All @types packages** updated to latest

### 🎨 UI Components & Libraries

- **All Radix UI components** updated to latest versions
- **Axios**: 1.8.4 → 1.10.0
- **Zod**: 3.24.2 → 3.25.74
- **Lucide React**: 0.483.0 → 0.525.0
- **React Day Picker**: 9.6.3 → 9.8.0
- **React Error Boundary**: 5.0.0 → 6.0.0

### 🔧 Code Quality Improvements

- Fixed TypeScript strict mode issues introduced by newer TypeScript version
- Resolved implicit "any" type parameters throughout codebase
- Removed `@million/lint` due to compatibility conflicts with security fixes
- Updated Next.js configuration accordingly

### 📋 Deferred Updates

The following packages were intentionally **not** updated to avoid potential breaking changes:

- **Jest** (29.x → 30.x): Major version - requires testing framework validation
- **Sonner** (1.x → 2.x): Toast library - potential API changes
- **TailwindCSS** (3.x → 4.x): CSS framework - risk of styling breaks
- **Recharts** (2.x → 3.x): Charts library - likely API changes

These can be addressed in separate PRs with proper UI/functionality testing.

### ✅ Verification

- ✅ `npm audit` shows **0 vulnerabilities** (down from 5)
- ✅ All TypeScript compilation errors resolved
- ✅ Dependencies properly updated in package.json and package-lock.json
- ✅ No breaking changes to existing functionality

### 🎯 Impact

This update provides:
- **Enhanced security** with all known vulnerabilities patched
- **Latest features** from React 19.1, Next.js 15.3.5, and other packages
- **Improved developer experience** with updated tooling
- **Better type safety** with stricter TypeScript enforcement
- **Maintained stability** by avoiding risky major version jumps

The changes are minimal and surgical, focusing on security and compatibility while preserving existing functionality.

author: infinityrobot
body:
> [!IMPORTANT] 
> **Note!** This PR is branched off and is dependent on the Cohere `Provider` implementation in https://github.com/crmne/ruby_llm/pull/275.
> Reranking has been submitted as a separate contribution to allow for a meaningful review independent of the core Cohere `Provider` implementation. The diff here might be a bit complicated until the core Cohere implementation is approved.

## What this does

> [!NOTE]
> This PR adds support for reranking to RubyLLM, enabling semantic reranking of search results and document collections. The initial implementation supports Cohere's [Rerank](https://cohere.com/rerank) models.

### Why add reranking?

Reranking is a standard step in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines that bridges retrieval and generation workflows. It's not application-specific logic but rather a foundational communication pattern with LLMs that most users implementing search, recommendation, or RAG systems will need.

Reranking broadly serves multiple common use cases:

- **RAG** – Improving context relevance before chat-based text generation
- **Search enhancement** – Semantically ranking search results
- **Recommendation systems** – Ordering items by relevance to user queries
- **Content curation** – Ranking documents, articles, or responses by semantic similarity

### Implementation overview

The reranking implementation is primarily via a new `RubyLLM::Rerank` class which operates via a pattern that mirrors that of the current `RubyLLM::Embedding` implementation.

> [!NOTE]
> To facilitate easy reranking, a `default_rerank_model` attribute has been added to `Configuration` which is set to Cohere's `rerank-v3.5`.


The main entry point is `RubyLLM.rerank(...)` which delegates to `RubyLLM::Rerank.rank(...)`. This method accepts:
  - `query` – The search query to evaluate documents against
  - `documents` – An array of text documents to rerank
  - Optional reranking parameters
    - `top_n` – Top number of results to return
    - `max_tokens_per_doc` – Max tokens per doc for chunking
  - Optional model parameters (per embeddings an other implementations)
    - `model`, `provider`, , `context`, `assume_model_exists`

Using the `Provider` `Reranking` interface – e.g., `RubyLLM::Providers::Cohere::Reranking` – the API payload with the query, documents, and parameters are prepared and submitted.

If successful, the response is parsed and a `Rerank` object is returned with:
  - `model` – The ID of the model used
  - `results` – The results of the reranking, returned as an array of `RerankResult` objects sorted by `relevance_score` containing:
    - `index` – The original `document` index in `documents`
    - `relevance_score` – Score between 0-1 with 1 being perfectly relevant
    - `document` – The document content tested
  - `search_units` – The billable units returned by providers like Cohere, TogetherAI, etc.

### Usage example

```ruby
# Configure your API key
RubyLLM.configure do |config|
  config.cohere_api_key = ENV['COHERE_API_KEY']
end

# Your search query
query = "How do I handle exceptions in Ruby?"

# Candidate documents to rerank
documents = [
  "Ruby uses begin/rescue/end blocks to handle exceptions, similar to try/catch in other languages.",
  "JavaScript async/await syntax makes handling asynchronous operations much easier.",
  "The raise keyword in Ruby allows you to throw custom exceptions with specific error messages.",
  "Python dictionaries are similar to Ruby hashes but use different syntax for iteration.",
  "Ruby's ensure block always executes, making it perfect for cleanup operations like closing files."
]

# Rerank the documents
RubyLLM.rerank(query, documents)
=>
#<RubyLLM::Rerank:0x0000000122cb0d68
 @model="rerank-v3.5",
 @results=
  [#<RubyLLM::RerankResult:0x0000000122cb0ed0
    @document="Ruby uses begin/rescue/end blocks to handle exceptions, similar to try/catch in other languages.",
    @index=0,
    @relevance_score=0.8865877>,
   #<RubyLLM::RerankResult:0x0000000122cb0e80
    @document="The raise keyword in Ruby allows you to throw custom exceptions with specific error messages.",
    @index=2,
    @relevance_score=0.63750535>,
   #<RubyLLM::RerankResult:0x0000000122cb0e58
    @document="Ruby's ensure block always executes, making it perfect for cleanup operations like closing files.",
    @index=4,
    @relevance_score=0.08234999>,
   #<RubyLLM::RerankResult:0x0000000122cb0e30
    @document="JavaScript async/await syntax makes handling asynchronous operations much easier.",
    @index=1,
    @relevance_score=0.031288605>,
   #<RubyLLM::RerankResult:0x0000000122cb0e08
    @document="Python dictionaries are similar to Ruby hashes but use different syntax for iteration.",
    @index=3,
    @relevance_score=0.027483363>],
 @search_units=1>
```

### Implementation notes

- Follows existing RubyLLM patterns for model communication
- Added detailed documentation in `docs/guides/rerank.md`
- Includes comprehensive error handling and response validation
- Supports all Cohere Rerank model variants (`rerank-v3.5`, `rerank-english-v3.0`, `rerank-multilingual-v3.0`, etc.)
- Ready to support other ranking providers – e.g., existing Ollama models or in case of potential new providers that offer a Rerank API like [TogetherAI](https://docs.together.ai/docs/rerank-overview)
- Maintains consistency with existing RubyLLM conventions
- Supports context-specific implementations (e.g., `rerank_context.rerank(...)`)
- Full specs with VCRs

body:
## Summary

Batch of somewhat interrelated v6 followups:
- When recalling all ref images, clear all current ref images. When recalling a single ref image, it is added instead.
- Fix an issue where new images would be inserted into the search results for gallery in the wrong position.
- Make the gallery scroll-into-view logic more resilient.
- Separate Generate tab width/height/aspect from Canvas Bbox width/height/aspect, allowing users to change it independently of Canvas's size (and change it while Canvas is staging)
  - Extract aspect ratio constants from the canvas reducers
  - Copy the relevant state and reducer logic from Canvas to Params slice
  - Copy relevant components from Canvas to Generate tab left panel
  - Rework graph builders to reference the correct size state depending on tab, this started to get really hairy and I ended up simplifying a few things w/ graph builders generally.
- Fixed an issue where certain metadata values (booleans, null/undefined, empty strings) might not render anything in the metadata actions list. You'd get a label and recall button but no value.
- When no metadata has no negative prompt and it is recalled, recall it as `null`, disabling negative prompt.
- When progress percentage is zero, show the progress bar as pulsing instead of totally empty. Sometimes we are at 0% for a few seconds, and it looks like the app has stalled. Now, during generation, the progress bar is always either pulsing or filled up at least a tiny bit.
- Fixed an issue with staging session internal data which could cause an error. The error is only visible on the JS console - didn't crash the app - but it could result in invalid progress data.
- Add special handling for FLUX Kontext dev ref image models. When we use FLUX Kontext dev is used, the ref image model must be the same model as the main model. 
- Improve ref image preview styling, especially for error states.
- Fix an issue where invalid ref image state wasn't detected.
- Fixed a possible cause of this error:
    ```
    [2025-07-04 11:38:41,771]::[InvokeAI]::ERROR --> Traceback (most recent call last):
      File "/mnt/AI/InvokeAI3/src/invokeai/app/services/session_processor/session_processor_default.py", line 435, in _process
        self._queue_item = self._invoker.services.session_queue.dequeue()
                          ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

                      ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

        total = sum(row[1] for row in counts_result)
                ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

    ```

## Related Issues / Discussions

Feedback from discord

I had to make a lot of small changes to graph builder logic. I tested Generate tab and each generation mode on Canvas, with every supported local model arch. I think everything is working but it's possible I missed something.

author: arun-muthuraman
body:
The current implementation decodes the column count in `RowBinaryWithNamesAndTypes` format as a single byte, which fails when the number of queried columns exceeds 127, raising an ArgumentError.
`(ArgumentError) failed to decode "" as ClickHouse type (no function clause matching in Ch.Types.decode/3)`

According to the [ClickHouse RowBinaryWithNamesAndTypes specification](https://clickhouse.com/docs/en/interfaces/formats/RowBinaryWithNamesAndTypes), the column count should be encoded as a multi-byte varint.

This PR fixes this bug by using varint patterns instead of single-byte decoding for column counts in `decode_rows/1` and `decode_names_and_rows/1` functions.

Adding fix on behalf on IBM AIX 
This is related assignment of compound_variables. 

Below is the example test case to assign compond_variable 
using set-x to display the values. 

```
set -x

complex=( real=1 img=2 )
+ complex.real=1
+ complex.img=2

complex=( real1=3 img1=4 )
+ complex.real1=3
+ complex.img1=4

RC=$?

real=`echo "${complex.real}"`

img=`echo "${complex.img}"`
+ echo ''

real1=`echo "${complex.real1}"`
+ echo 3
+ real1=3

img1=`echo "${complex.img1}"`
+ echo 4
+ img1=4

author: pocketninja
body:
Proposed fix for Issue #142 

When a stored value for a feature is `0` (JSON `"0"`), `$filtered->value('value')` internally makes a loose comparison of `"0" == true`, resulting in no matches being found. 

`null` is then passed into `json_decode()`, triggering the following:

```
   DEPRECATED  json_decode(): Passing null to parameter #1 ($json) of type string is deprecated in vendor/laravel/pennant/src/Drivers/DatabaseDriver.php on line 161.


   JsonException  Syntax error.
```

Issue was reproduced with tests pre-solve.

The fix assumes that if `$filtered` has records which match the provided `$feature` and `$scope` it can just grab the value directly from `->first()` - that would typically have one result I believe.

author: genmini-ai
body:
## Overview
This PR implements a comprehensive adversarial evaluation testing system that validates the robustness of our AI-powered presentation evaluation by applying 5 different types of adversarial attacks and measuring their impact on evaluation scores.

## 🛡️ Adversarial Attack Types Implemented

### 1. **Beautiful Nonsense** 
- **Attack**: Replaces scientific/technical content with surrealist art references and poetic language
- **Purpose**: Tests if evaluator can detect content relevance issues
- **Example**: "Machine learning algorithms" → "Melting clocks dance through neural pathways"

### 2. **Fact Flip**
- **Attack**: Inverts factual claims and flips numerical values  
- **Purpose**: Tests factual accuracy detection capabilities
- **Example**: "95% accuracy" → "5% accuracy", "beneficial effects" → "harmful effects"

### 3. **Logical Chaos**
- **Attack**: Randomly shuffles slide order to break logical flow
- **Purpose**: Tests narrative structure and coherence evaluation
- **Example**: Conclusion slides appearing before introduction

### 4. **Swiss Cheese** 
- **Attack**: Randomly deletes critical content chunks (20-40%)
- **Purpose**: Tests completeness and content coverage detection
- **Example**: Removing key methodology sections or important data

### 5. **Gradual Decay**
- **Attack**: Progressive quality degradation across multiple dimensions
- **Purpose**: Tests sensitivity to subtle quality reductions
- **Example**: Gradually increasing typos, formatting issues, and content gaps

## 🔬 Evaluation Impact Analysis

The system measures attack effectiveness by:

- **Score Drop Analysis**: Quantifies how much each attack reduces evaluation scores
- **Success Rate Tracking**: Percentage of attacks that successfully fool the evaluator  
- **Dimension Vulnerability**: Which evaluation aspects (visual, content, structure) are most vulnerable
- **Robustness Classification**: 
  - 🟢 **HIGH** (mean drop < 0.1): Evaluation is robust to attacks
  - 🟡 **MODERATE** (mean drop 0.1-0.5): Some vulnerability detected
  - 🔴 **LOW** (mean drop > 0.5): Evaluation system is vulnerable

## 🧪 Testing Framework

### Core Components
- `src/opencanvas/evaluation/adversarial_attacks.py` - Attack implementation
- `src/opencanvas/evaluation/analysis.py` - Statistical analysis framework
- `tests/test_adversarial_evaluation.py` - Testing orchestration
- `run_adversarial_eval_test.py` - CLI runner for adversarial tests

### Usage
```bash
# Run adversarial evaluation tests
python run_adversarial_eval_test.py

# Generate fresh presentations and test
python run_adversarial_eval_test.py --regenerate

# Analysis only (skip testing)
python run_adversarial_eval_test.py --analysis-only
```

### Output Structure
test_output/adversarial_analysis/
├── adversarial_evaluation_results.json # Raw test results
├── analysis_report.json # Statistical analysis
├── attacked_presentations/ # Modified HTML files
├── attacked_evaluations/ # Individual eval results
└── plots/ # Visualization charts

body:
Refactored and optimized key components of the Vision Wagon system:

- Database (`database.py`):
    - Corrected usage of SQLAlchemy asynchronous API (select, execute).
    - Optimized `get_system_stats` to use direct SQL aggregate queries.
    - Added missing Content CRUD methods used by AssemblyAgent.
- Orchestrator (`orchestrator.py`):
    - Optimized task queue management with a lookup dictionary for pending tasks.
    - Refactored task execution logic into smaller, more manageable methods.
    - Implemented parallel health checks for registered agents.
    - Improved handling of task cancellation for tasks in the queue.
- Main Application (`main.py`):
    - Ensured consistent registration of defined and imported agents.
- Project Structure:
    - Removed redundant Nginx and Prometheus configuration files from the project root.
    - Clarified logging directory usage (removed .gitkeep from vision_wagon/logs).

These changes aim to improve code correctness, efficiency, and maintainability.

It caches the data so that if it is less than 24 hours old, we do not recall the API. I kept it to the latest day of data available, but if we need historical I can change the script.

Our Methodology is :

Our APR is calculated using a TVL-weighted median of pool-level APRs. Each pool represents a payment rail (e.g., Venmo, Zelle, Wise). Our APR calculatiuon can be found here https://docs.zkp2p.xyz/user-guides/for-sellers/calculating-apr.

This is then rolled up and should give the Median APY as suggested by your docs.

Let me know if you need more info.

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

The symbol package validation for `Cratis.Chronicle.Api` was failing with the error:

> The uploaded symbols package contains pdb(s) for a corresponding dll(s) not found in the nuget package.

This prevented the symbol package from being published to NuGet Gallery.

## Root Cause

The `Api.csproj` used a custom build process with manual SDK imports but lacked the ILRepack integration that `DotNET.csproj` has. When repacking was enabled (`Repack=true`), the symbol files (PDB) didn't match the merged assemblies because:

1. The Api project manually copied DLL files but not PDB files during dependency building
2. The Api project wasn't using ILRepack's symbol handling capabilities
3. The repacking process wasn't preserving debug information properly

## Solution

**Added ILRepack integration to Api.csproj:**
- Added `ILRepackTargetsFile` property pointing to `../ILRepack.targets`
- Added `ILRepack.Lib.MSBuild.Task` package reference with proper asset configuration
- Added `DoNotInternalize` configuration for Connections assembly to match DotNET.csproj behavior

**Fixed BuildDependencies target:**
- Modified to copy both DLL and PDB files from DotNET build output
- Added conditional copy for PDB files with existence check

**Updated target framework handling:**
- Made `EmbedXmlDocs` target use `$(TargetFramework)` instead of hardcoded framework version
- Updated ILRepack.targets to use `$(TargetFramework)` for consistent tool execution

## Verification

The fix ensures that:
- ✅ Api project builds successfully with `Repack=false` (development mode)
- ✅ Api project builds successfully with `Repack=true` (release mode)
- ✅ PDB file (`Cratis.Chronicle.Api.pdb`) is correctly generated during repacking
- ✅ ILRepack process properly handles symbol files with `DebugInfo="true"`

When the Api package is built with repacking enabled, the symbol files will now correctly match the merged assembly structure, resolving the NuGet symbol package validation error.

Fixes #1907.

author: oursin
body:
## What?

This PR adds support for setting the authority pseudo-header when sending gRPC requests.

## Why?

This MR is similar to #3454, which was not accepted because the feature was supposed to work without changes using the `dns://authority/endpoint` syntax.

The company I work at uses gRPC services with TLS certificates matching the gRPC service name. So for example we would have a gRPC service `company.test.v1` hosted on a machine reachable from `test-v1.internal.company.com`, but exposing a certificate signed for `company.test.v1`.

I tried using the `dns:///` syntax like this:

```js
client.connect('dns://company.test.v1/test-v1.internal.company.com:443', {timeout: '5s', tls: TLSParams});
```

But I end up with this error, the same as if I was simply trying to connect without the `dns:///` syntax.

```
context deadline exceeded: connection error: desc = "transport: authentication handshake failed: tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate is valid for company.test.v1, not test-v1.internal.company.com
```

I have a workaround by configuring my `/etc/hosts` file so that the addess in `connect` is company.test.v1 but I would prefer if it was a k6 parameter directly.

With the changes made in this MR i can connect like this:

```js
client.connect('test-v1.internal.company.com:443', {timeout: '5s', authority: 'company.test.v1', tls: TLSParams});
```

Which allows the TLS handshake to work properly.

author: ksylvan
body:
# Improved Anthropic Plugin Configuration Logic 

## Summary

This PR improves the vendor configuration logic for the Anthropic plugin by adding proper configuration validation and enhancing OAuth token management. The changes ensure that vendors are only added to the active vendor manager when they are properly configured and introduce automatic OAuth flow handling for the Anthropic client.

## Related Issues

Closes #1589 

## Files Changed

- **`core/plugin_registry.go`**: Modified the `ConfigureVendors()` method to add an additional validation check
- **`plugins/ai/anthropic/anthropic.go`**: Added configuration validation logic and improved OAuth handling

## Code Changes

### core/plugin_registry.go
```go
// Before
if vendorErr := vendor.Configure(); vendorErr == nil {
    o.VendorManager.AddVendors(vendor)
}

// After  
if vendorErr := vendor.Configure(); vendorErr == nil && vendor.IsConfigured() {
    o.VendorManager.AddVendors(vendor)
}
```

### plugins/ai/anthropic/anthropic.go
- Added `vendorTokenIdentifier` constant set to "claude"
- Simplified API key setup question logic by removing conditional required flag based on OAuth setting
- Added comprehensive `IsConfigured()` method that:
  - Validates API key configuration
  - Handles OAuth token validation with 5-minute buffer
  - Automatically triggers OAuth flow when needed
  - Provides user feedback during authentication process

## Reason for Changes

These changes address configuration validation issues where vendors could be added to the active manager even when not properly configured. The previous logic only checked if the `Configure()` method executed without errors, but didn't verify that the vendor actually had valid credentials or configuration.

For the Anthropic plugin specifically, this resolves OAuth flow management by automatically handling token validation and renewal, improving the user experience when using OAuth authentication.

## Impact of Changes

- **Improved reliability**: Vendors will only be activated when they have valid configuration
- **Better user experience**: OAuth users will have automatic token validation and renewal
- **Reduced errors**: Prevents misconfigured vendors from being used in the application
- **Enhanced security**: Proper token validation with time-based checks

## Test Plan

- Test vendor configuration with valid API keys
- Test vendor configuration with invalid/missing API keys  
- Test OAuth flow with valid tokens
- Test OAuth flow with expired tokens (should trigger automatic renewal)
- Test OAuth flow with no existing tokens (should prompt for authentication)
- Verify that only properly configured vendors appear in the active vendor manager

## Additional Notes

The `IsConfigured()` method includes a 5-minute buffer for OAuth token validation, which provides a reasonable margin for token expiration handling. The automatic OAuth flow trigger improves usability by eliminating the need for manual token management.

**Potential considerations:**
- The automatic OAuth flow in `IsConfigured()` could potentially block if the OAuth server is unreachable
- Console output during OAuth flow may not be appropriate in all execution contexts
- The hardcoded 5-minute buffer for token validation may need adjustment based on actual token lifetimes

author: dragonatorul
body:
## Summary

This PR introduces optional multi-tenant support with FastMCP-inspired bearer token authentication and includes a critical Unicode parameter substitution fix for FalkorDB.

### Key Features

- **Multi-Tenant Support**: Optional feature flag based multi-tenancy (`ENABLE_MULTI_TENANCY`)
- **Bearer Token Auth**: JWT bearer token authentication with JWKS validation
- **Tenant Graph Isolation**: Prefix-based graph naming (`${tenantId}_${graphName}`)
- **Unicode Bug Fix**: Parameter substitution workaround for broken FalkorDB JavaScript client
- **Zero Breaking Changes**: Fully backward compatible with existing API

### Technical Implementation

**Authentication Modes**:

## Summary

This PR integrates audiocore's export functionality with the processor actions and significantly simplifies the audiocore architecture by removing redundant components.

### Changes

#### 1. **Audiocore Export Integration**
- Added capture manager field to Processor with thread-safe setter/getter
- Modified `StartAudioCoreCapture` to return adapter for manager access  
- Updated `DatabaseAction` to use audiocore's `ExportClip` when enabled
- Implemented graceful fallback to myaudio when audiocore is unavailable

#### 2. **Architecture Simplification** 
- Removed redundant `CaptureHandler` and tests (-630 lines)
- Eliminated dual buffer writing in `myaudio_compat` adapter
- Simplified `DatabaseAction` by removing complex fallback logic
- Updated integration tests to test export functionality directly

### Benefits

- **Single Export Path**: Processor → CaptureManager → Export (no duplication)
- **Reduced Memory Usage**: No more duplicate buffering between systems
- **Cleaner Architecture**: Clear separation - processor decides when, audiocore handles how
- **Less Code**: Removed 630 lines of redundant export handling
- **Better Performance**: Eliminated unnecessary buffer copies and conversions

### Testing

- ✅ All processor tests pass
- ✅ All audiocore integration tests pass  
- ✅ No linting issues
- ✅ Maintains backward compatibility with myaudio

### Configuration

To enable audiocore export:
```yaml
audio:
  useaudiocore: true
```

When enabled, the processor will use audiocore's enhanced export capabilities for saving detection clips.

author: copilot
body:
## Summary

This PR adds SMS autocomplete functionality to the `NzInputOtpComponent` by introducing a new `nzAutoComplete` input property that enables the HTML `autocomplete="one-time-code"` attribute on mobile devices.

## Problem

The existing `NzInputOtpComponent` didn't support SMS auto-fill functionality on mobile devices, requiring users to manually type OTP codes even when they received them via SMS. This created a poor user experience on mobile platforms where browsers can automatically suggest OTP codes from SMS messages.

## Solution

Added a new `nzAutoComplete` boolean input property that:
- Adds `autocomplete="one-time-code"` attribute to the first input field when enabled
- Enhances input handling to detect and distribute multi-character autocomplete input across all OTP fields
- Maintains backward compatibility (defaults to `false`)
- Works seamlessly with existing features (formatter, mask, length, etc.)

## Usage

```typescript
// Enable SMS autocomplete
<nz-input-otp [nzAutoComplete]="true"></nz-input-otp>

// Works with all existing features
<nz-input-otp 
  [nzAutoComplete]="true" 
  [nzFormatter]="uppercase"
  [nzMask]="'*'"
  [nzLength]="6">
</nz-input-otp>
```

## Key Features

- ✅ **Standards Compliant**: Uses HTML standard `autocomplete="one-time-code"` attribute
- ✅ **Mobile Optimized**: Enables SMS auto-fill on iOS and Android browsers  
- ✅ **Backward Compatible**: Opt-in feature that doesn't affect existing implementations
- ✅ **Feature Complete**: Works with formatter, mask, custom length, and all existing properties
- ✅ **Smart Distribution**: Automatically distributes autocomplete input across all fields
- ✅ **Comprehensive Testing**: 6 new test cases covering various scenarios

## Changes Made

### Core Implementation
- Added `@Input() nzAutoComplete: boolean = false` property with `booleanAttribute` transformer
- Enhanced template with conditional `[attr.autocomplete]` binding on first input only
- Modified `onInput()` method to detect multi-character autocomplete input
- Added `handleMultiCharacterInput()` method to distribute characters across fields

### Testing
- Added 6 comprehensive test cases covering:
  - Attribute setting behavior when enabled/disabled
  - Multi-character input handling on first field
  - Integration with formatter and mask features
  - Proper handling of non-first input fields

### Documentation
- Updated demo with autocomplete examples
- Enhanced API documentation in both English and Chinese
- Updated component description to mention SMS auto-completion support

### Demo Updates
- Added "With AutoComplete (SMS Support)" example
- Added combined example showing autocomplete with formatter and mask
- Updated documentation descriptions

## Testing

Manual testing confirmed:
- Autocomplete attribute is properly set only on the first input when enabled
- Multi-character input is correctly distributed across all fields
- Existing functionality remains unchanged when autocomplete is disabled
- All existing features work correctly with autocomplete enabled

## Browser Support

This feature leverages the standard HTML `autocomplete="one-time-code"` attribute, which is supported by:
- iOS Safari (iOS 12+)
- Chrome on Android
- Other modern mobile browsers that support SMS OTP suggestions

Fixes #9247.

Add integration tests to reproduce a replica cache invalidation bug where canister deployment tasks are not re-executed after a replica restart.

The current caching mechanism incorrectly serves cached results for canister deployment and other replica-dependent tasks even after the Pocket-IC replica has been reset (e.g., by restarting the server), preventing actual re-deployment. These tests are designed to fail with the existing behavior, clearly demonstrating that tasks relying on replica state are not properly invalidated. A `REPLICA_CACHE_BUG.md` file is also included to detail the bug.

The changes include updates to metadata for better mobile and SEO support, restructuring of routes and components, and the addition of new features like a collaborators section and structured data for SEO.

### Metadata and SEO Improvements:
* Updated `public/index.html` to include mobile-specific meta tags (`apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style`, `apple-mobile-web-app-title`) and an Apple touch icon.
* Enhanced the `SEO` component in `src/components/SEO.jsx` to support additional meta tags (keywords, robots, author) and structured data for better search engine optimization.
* Integrated the `SEO` component into key pages like `Home` and `Organizer` to provide page-specific metadata. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3f516fbdeb9a7ec0382eddb852845968f9cdaa1cff026ac0ce8fdf1fd351cc17R9-R37) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7fa2ef835cc2d5b64ce48eace2bf1fab89eca8d1553d2a1fbf4a01ddbc378170R4)

body:
This pull request introduces several enhancements and optimizations across the codebase, focusing on Docker configuration, environment handling, dependency updates, and logging improvements. The most significant changes include refactoring the `Dockerfile` for better build efficiency, introducing an `EnvironmentHelper` module to dynamically display the current environment in the UI, updating Ruby and Alpine versions, and improving logging in the `entrypoint.sh` script.

This update will also pull in the latest version of the Common Styles gem which contains the updated Google Tag ID changes specific to [ticket 154](https://github.com/epimorphics/hmlr-linked-data/issues/154) 

### Docker and Build Configuration:
* Refactored `Dockerfile` to optimize build efficiency by introducing multi-stage builds, defaulting environment variables (`RUBY_VERSION=3.4.4`, `ALPINE_VERSION=3.22`, `BUNDLER_VERSION=2.6.9`), and refining network settings. Added caching improvements with `apk add --no-cache`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-dd2c0eb6ea5cfc6c4bd4eac30934e2d5746747af48fef6da689e85b752f39557L1-R57) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-dd2c0eb6ea5cfc6c4bd4eac30934e2d5746747af48fef6da689e85b752f39557L59-R80)
* Updated `Makefile` to align with new Docker defaults, including `RUN_VARS` for container execution options. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-76ed074a9305c04054cdebb9e9aad2d818052b07091de1f20cad0bbac34ffb52L4-R4) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-76ed074a9305c04054cdebb9e9aad2d818052b07091de1f20cad0bbac34ffb52R14) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-76ed074a9305c04054cdebb9e9aad2d818052b07091de1f20cad0bbac34ffb52L83-R84)

### Environment Handling:

author: drryanhuang
body: ### PR描述 ```python # 文件位置 fastdeploy/model_executor/ops/gpu/fastdeploy_ops.py @unified def static_op_extract_text_token_output(max_seq_len,max_seq_len_index,mm_token_num_len,seq_lens_this_time,cu_seqlens_q,score_text): # The output variable's dtype use default value 'float32', # and the actual dtype of output variable will be inferred in runtime. if in_dynamic_or_pir_mode(): outs = _C_ops._run_custom_op("static_op_extract_text_token_output", max_seq_len,max_seq_len_index,mm_token_num_len,seq_lens_this_time,cu_seqlens_q,score_text) res = [] start_idx = 0 res.append(outs[start_idx]) start_idx += 1 print("static_op_extract_text_token_output op original res is: ", res) return res[0] if len(res)==1 else res ``` 上述生成的 `static_op_extract_text_token_output` 函数实现中，存在对输出结果根据长度进行解包的逻辑： 当输出结果为单元素列表时，直接返回该元素，否则返回完整的列表。 这种逻辑导致了动态图与静态图模式下接口返回值类型不一致的问题。 在SOT转静执行过程（包括模拟）中，返回值始终经过上述解包处理； 而在动态图模式下，原始实现直接返回底层C++扩展算子的输出，所以我们做进一步处理： ```python # 文件位置 fastdeploy/import_ops.py @functools.wraps(original_custom_op) def unified_op(*args, **kwargs): if paddle.in_dynamic_mode(): res = original_cpp_ext_op(*args, **kwargs) if res is None: return None # TODO(DrRyanHuang): Remove this if when we align the implementation of custom op and C++ extension if isinstance(res, list) and len(res) == 1: return res[0] return res ``` cc @SigureMo ----- **UPDATE 2025.07.11** 记录一下解决BUG的过程，略有曲折，算是一个比较难排查的BUG吧： 开启SOT后报： ``` Error: /workspace/Paddle/paddle/phi/kernels/gpu/embedding_kernel.cu:41 Assertion `id < N` failed. Id should smaller than 103424 but received an id value: 12884901890. Error: /workspace/Paddle/paddle/phi/kernels/gpu/embedding_kernel.cu:41 Assertion `id < N` failed. Id should smaller than 103424 but received an id value: 11712375818919. ``` 我们把 Embedding 的输出打出来看： ``` ids_remove_padding: Tensor(shape=[969], dtype=int64, place=Place(gpu:0), stop_gradient=True, [706 , 12884901890 , 11712375818919, 11712375818919, 4726599895656434343, 100273 , 3165 , 23 , 2969 , 93963 , 50343 , 93919 , 4 , 93963 , 101304 , 100295 , 100295 , 100295 , 100295 , 100295 , ``` 发现出现了很多莫名其妙的**大数** 和动态图对比了一下，本来应该为 -1 的每行第0个位置，变成了这些大数 我们知道，动态图第一列的数据相当于 mask，如果是 -1，说明当前只跑了一条数据，而为何SOT这里就会是一个很大的数呢? 还有个实验现象：开测试脚本为1条的时候，就没问题，开测试脚本为2条的时候，就会出现这个问题，我们起先认为是 slice 的问题 我们打印了 Embedding 的结果，发现第一次进入主循环是正常的，在第二次开始，就会有很多大数出现（但此时没报错） 第一次的输出也就是第二次的输入，这个过程有问题 从自定义算子 `update_inputs` 中找到了给第 0 列赋值的位置： https://github.com/PaddlePaddle/FastDeploy/blob/c08561c13add98584040271f6f5bea4eb925ca85/custom_ops/gpu_ops/update_inputs.cu#L48-L60 第60行会将 `next_tokens` 数据复制到 `input_ids_now` 的第0列，那现在就有两种可能了，要么 `next_tokens` 数据有问题，要么就是 `input_ids_now` 没被赋值，（看前面随机出现的大数，倾向于这个） 如果是没被赋值，看上面的if条件 `thread_idx < bsz` 除非 bsz=1，即使我们传入多条数据，也依旧只会给第一行赋值 也就是无论数据多少条，都会只取第一条，那很大概率就是存在没考虑到的 slice 或者 索引操作 这时 @zyfncg 建议开 `FLAGS_print_ir` 打印一下 program 看看，并建议**倒**着看，可惜开发机环境崩了，没办法展示log了 从log中可以很明显的看出，存在一个只取第一个元素的操作，也就是： https://github.com/PaddlePaddle/FastDeploy/blob/f6ffbc3cbd89bb9d6a8f1e5f0015db3b94a37cd4/fastdeploy/model_executor/models/ernie4_5_vl/ernie4_5_vl_moe.py#L441-L448 不对啊，之前和 @xiaoxiaohehe001 一起看过这个自定义算子的 infer_meta： https://github.com/PaddlePaddle/FastDeploy/blob/f6ffbc3cbd89bb9d6a8f1e5f0015db3b94a37cd4/custom_ops/gpu_ops/extract_text_token_output.cu#L74-L83 他明明返回的是一个list啊? 我取0号元素，不就是把Tensor拿出来吗？怎么会是对Tensor做索引操作呢? FastDeploy 中，动态图走 C++ extension ，静态图选择自定义算子，逻辑如下： https://github.com/PaddlePaddle/FastDeploy/blob/f6ffbc3cbd89bb9d6a8f1e5f0015db3b94a37cd4/fastdeploy/import_ops.py#L78-L81 回到 Github PR Description 开头的自定义算子（静态图用），这里会做一个解包的操作： `return res[0] if len(res)==1 else res`，如果返回值列表中只有一个元素，则直接返回该元素 而在动态图中由于没有这解包操作，所以需要手动在后面添加一个 `[0]` 的索引操作 所以，当跑SOT转静的时候，做了两次取0号元素的，所以会始终出现上述问题 这个PR只是在当前算子体系下加了个补丁，后续应该规范算子，C++层面统一返回 vector，而不是既有 `vector` 又有 `Tensor` 感谢 @zyfncg @SigureMo 和我一起排查

body:
See https://github.com/cvmfs/cvmfs/issues/3901

What seemed to work until recently now fails:

	incus launch --vm images:debian/12 cvmfs-server-fstab-issue
	incus exec cvmfs-server-fstab-issue -- bash -l <EOF
	apt install -y wget && wget http://cvmrepo.s3.cern.ch/cvmrepo/apt/cvmfs-release-latest_all.deb && dpkg -i cvmfs-release-latest_all.deb && apt update && apt install -y cvmfs cvmfs-server && cvmfs_server mkfs -o root my.repo.name
	EOF

	...
	Warning: Failed to restart apache after enabling necessary modules
	Creating Configuration Files... done
	Creating CernVM-FS Master Key and Self-Signed Certificate... done
	Creating CernVM-FS Server Infrastructure... done
	Creating Backend Storage... done
	Signing 30 day whitelist with master key... done
	Creating Initial Repository... done
	Mounting CernVM-FS Storage... (overlayfs) mount: /var/spool/cvmfs/my.repo.name/rdonly: wrong fs type, bad option, bad superblock on cvmfs2#my.repo.name, missing codepage or helper program, or other error.
	       dmesg(1) may have more information after failed mount system call.
	fail
	root@cvmfs-server-fstab-issue:~# cat /etc/fstab
	LABEL=rootfs  /         ext4  defaults  0 0
	LABEL=UEFI    /boot/efi vfat  defaults  0 0
	cvmfs2#my.repo.name /var/spool/cvmfs/my.repo.name/rdonly fuse allow_other,fsname=my.repo.name,config=/etc/cvmfs/repositories.d/my.repo.name/client.conf:/var/spool/cvmfs/my.repo.name/client.local,cvmfs_suid,noauto 0 0 # added by CernVM-FS for my.repo.name
	overlay_my.repo.name /cvmfs/my.repo.name overlay upperdir=/var/spool/cvmfs/my.repo.name/scratch/current,lowerdir=/var/spool/cvmfs/my.repo.name/rdonly,workdir=/var/spool/cvmfs/my.repo.name/ofs_workdir,noauto,nodev,ro 0 0 # added by CernVM-FS for my.repo.name

dmesg says:

	fuse: Unknown parameter 'fsname'

`cvmfs2#` prefix in the first field, which is called deprecated by mount(8) and fstab(5).

Third field (with value fuse) gives mount an indication of which helper program to call. Says fuse, with no subtype (i'd expect fuse.cvmfs). cvmfs installs `mount.cvmfs`, so let's use `cvmfs` as type.

Add support for ordinal date axes in line and bar charts to correctly display truncated or date-only fields.

This change introduces an ordinal scale for these specific date types, ensuring proper alignment and representation of discrete date intervals.

author: wmnjuguna
body:
## 🐛 Problem
The application was failing to start due to multiple issues in the `CategoryRepository`:

1. **Missing @Query Annotation Error:**
   ```
   PropertyReferenceException: No property 'findCategoryHierarchy' found for type 'Category'
   ```

2. **Repository-Service Type Mismatches:** Service methods expected `List<Category>` but repository methods were returning `Optional<Category>` for queries that logically return multiple results.

## 🔧 Changes Made

### 1. Fixed Return Type Mismatches
Updated repository methods to return appropriate collection types:

**BEFORE**
```java
Optional<Category> findByParentUuidIsNull();  // Root categories
Optional<Category> findByParentUuid(UUID uuid);  // Subcategories  
Optional<Category> findByIsActiveTrue();  // Active categories
```

**AFTER**
```java
List<Category> findByParentUuidIsNull();  // Root categories
List<Category> findByParentUuid(UUID uuid);  // Subcategories
List<Category> findByIsActiveTrue();  // Active categories
```

### 2. Added Custom Hierarchy Query
Implemented proper category hierarchy traversal with `@Query` annotation:

**BEFORE**
```java
List<Category> findCategoryHierarchy(UUID categoryUuid);  // No @Query annotation
```

**AFTER**
```java
@Query(value = """
        WITH RECURSIVE category_hierarchy AS (
            -- Base case: start with the given category
            SELECT uuid, name, description, parent_uuid, is_active, 
                   created_date, updated_date, created_by, updated_by, id, 0 as level
            FROM course_categories 
            WHERE uuid = :categoryUuid
            
            UNION ALL
            
            -- Recursive case: find all children
            SELECT c.uuid, c.name, c.description, c.parent_uuid, c.is_active,
                   c.created_date, c.updated_date, c.created_by, c.updated_by, c.id, ch.level + 1
            FROM course_categories c
            INNER JOIN category_hierarchy ch ON c.parent_uuid = ch.uuid
        )
        SELECT * FROM category_hierarchy
        ORDER BY level, name
        """, nativeQuery = true)
List<Category> findCategoryHierarchy(@Param("categoryUuid") UUID categoryUuid);
```

## 🎯 Root Cause Analysis

1. **Logical Inconsistency**: Repository methods for multi-result queries were using `Optional<Category>` instead of `List<Category>`
2. **Missing Custom Query**: Spring Data JPA couldn't derive query for complex hierarchy method name
3. **Service-Repository Mismatch**: Service layer expected collections but got optionals

## 🚀 Improvements Made

- **Logical Consistency**: Repository methods now return appropriate types for their use cases
- **Hierarchical Queries**: Proper recursive CTE implementation for category tree traversal
- **Performance**: Optimized hierarchy query with level ordering
- **Service Compatibility**: Repository signatures now match service layer expectations

## ✅ Impact

- ✅ Application now starts successfully
- ✅ Repository methods return logically correct types
- ✅ Category hierarchy queries work with proper recursion
- ✅ Service layer methods function as expected
- ✅ No breaking changes to public service interface

## 🧪 Affected Service Methods

The following service methods now work correctly:
- `getRootCategories()` - Returns list of root categories
- `getSubCategories(UUID)` - Returns list of subcategories
- `getActiveCategories()` - Returns list of active categories
- `getCategoryHierarchy(UUID)` - Returns hierarchical category tree

## 🧪 Testing

- [x] Application starts without PropertyReferenceException
- [x] Repository methods return correct collection types
- [x] Category hierarchy query executes successfully
- [x] Service layer methods work with updated repository signatures
- [ ] Integration tests for category hierarchy traversal (follow-up)

## 🔗 Related Issues

- Fixes application startup failure
- Part of broader repository query method standardization
- Enables proper category management functionality

## 📝 Commit Message

```
fix: correct CategoryRepository method signatures and add missing @Query annotation

- Change findByParentUuidIsNull() return type from Optional<Category> to List<Category>
- Change findByParentUuid() return type from Optional<Category> to List<Category>  
- Change findByIsActiveTrue() return type from Optional<Category> to List<Category>
- Add @Query annotation with recursive CTE for findCategoryHierarchy() method
- Implement proper category hierarchy traversal using PostgreSQL WITH RECURSIVE
- Ensure repository methods match service layer expectations

Resolves PropertyReferenceException and fixes Spring Boot application startup failure.
Repository methods now correctly return lists for multi-result queries and use explicit
queries for complex hierarchy operations.
```

body:
## Refactor: Enhanced Accessibility, Static Types, and Disabled Reason Tooltip for Button

### Overview

This PR introduces a set of improvements and refactors to the `<sp-button>` component and its base class, focused on accessibility, developer ergonomics, and user experience. The changes aim to make button states clearer and more robust, particularly around disabled and pending states.

---

### Changes Done

#### 1. **Type Improvements**
- Appended `as const` to `VALID_VARIANTS` and `VALID_STATIC_COLORS` to enforce stronger static typing for these value arrays.

#### 2. **Accessibility Enhancements**
- The button now sets `role="button"` by default if not already present.
- The `aria-disabled` attribute is dynamically updated in response to the button's `disabled` state.
- The `aria-busy` attribute is dynamically updated when the button is in a `pending` state.

#### 3. **Pending State Handling**
- The `pending` property is now consistently overridden in the `Button` class and handled with the proper decorator for reflection.
- The `click()` method now prevents interaction when the button is either `pending` or `disabled`.

#### 4. **Improved Disabled State Logic**
- Added a new `disabledReason` property. When set, the button will:
    - Use `aria-disabled` (instead of the native `disabled` attribute), keeping the button focusable for better accessibility.
    - Display a tooltip (`sp-tooltip`) with the provided reason when hovered.
- Introduced `isDisabled` getter to centralize logic for determining if the button is disabled (either via `disabled` or `disabledReason`).

#### 5. **Tooltip Integration**
- When `disabledReason` is present, an `sp-tooltip` is rendered above the button with the provided message to communicate to users why the button is disabled.

#### 6. **General Cleanups**
- Refactored and streamlined attribute reflection and property overrides.
- Updated event handlers to use the new `isDisabled` logic.
- Ensured all relevant ARIA attributes are updated in lifecycle hooks.

---

### Problem Solved

These changes address several usability and accessibility issues:

- **Accessibility**: By updating ARIA attributes (`aria-disabled`, `aria-busy`) and always providing a `role`, screen readers and assistive technologies can better interpret the button’s state.
- **User Feedback**: The new `disabledReason` property allows developers to communicate to users why an action is unavailable, improving user experience through contextual tooltips.
- **Developer Experience**: The use of `as const` and improved property typing results in safer, more predictable code, reducing potential bugs around allowed values for variants and static colors.
- **Consistency**: Centralized logic for disabled and pending states ensures consistent behavior and easier maintenance.

author: timmilesdw
body:
#### Overview

This PR improves the `scheduleManager` component by adding input validation, error handling, and thread safety.

#### What this PR does / why we need it

- Prevents adding schedule entries with empty crontab strings, logging an error instead.
- Handles and logs errors from invalid crontab expressions when adding new cron jobs.
- Adds a mutex to the `scheduleManager` to ensure thread-safe access to the internal entries map, preventing race conditions during concurrent operations.
- Updates and stabilizes tests to cover edge cases and concurrent usage.

When crontab is empty, we skip it and log error
```json
{"level":"error","msg":"crontab is empty","stacktrace": ... ,"time":"2025-07-04T19:39:28+03:00"}
```
When crontab is invalid, we skip it and log error
```json
{"level":"error","msg":"invalid crontab","crontab":"stub-crontab","stacktrace": ... ,"time":"2025-07-04T19:39:28+03:00"}
```

These changes make the scheduling logic more reliable and easier to maintain, and ensure that invalid or concurrent usage does not cause subtle bugs.

author: mcimadamore
body:
This PR adds check in `ReflectMethods` to issue errors when quotable methods, lambdas, method references are found inside an inner class. This includes member inner classes, local and anonymous inner classes, but static inner classes (sometimes referred to as *nested classes*) are ok. The issue is that if we allowed code reflection in these places, we would need to come up with uniform treatment for compiler-generated captured symbols. Currently `ReflectMethods` just allows method in an inner class to refer to a variable or a method in the enclosing class freely. While this is correct from a source code perspective, by the time we translate to bytecode, such references are no longer possible, and are typically mediated by compiler-generated symbols such as `this$0`. So, instead of generating a code model that might be unreliable, it is better, for now, to just disallow such cases. In principle, we should just "skip over" code elements we cannot support, and generate bytecode as usual. Indeed this is where I started, but then I realized that the support for lambda conversion into `Quoted` does not make sense unless we enable code reflection (as there's no real functional interface target we can use there). For this reason, an error is generated instead. --------- ### Progress - [x] Change must not contain extraneous whitespace ### Reviewers * [Paul Sandoz](https://openjdk.org/census#psandoz) (@PaulSandoz - **Reviewer**) ### Reviewing

author: russelldj
body:
This closes #133. This issue arises when `tree_crown_gdf_filtered` has no rows. The problem happens in this [line](https://github.com/open-forest-observatory/tree-detection-framework/blob/0c6d4aee76e6406f6835b20c7db703b5979220ad/tree_detection_framework/detection/detector.py#L797) where we check for crowns having valid geometry, non-zero area, and being polygon type. If there are no rows, the result of `apply` has `geometry` type rather than `bool`. I guess since the function doesn't have anything to run on, the type of the series (which is empty) defaults to the type of the original geometry column. For some reason, this causes all the columns to be dropped, which leads to indexing errors later.

This explicitly computes a boolean series. When indexing with the `valid_rows` variable, all columns are retained, even if no rows are.

## Overview

This PR significantly expands the test coverage for VStore by adding **10 new comprehensive test methods**, bringing the total from 23 to 33 test methods. The expansion addresses gaps in testing for configuration parameters, large datasets, advanced metadata filtering, error handling, and edge cases.

## What's Added

### 🧪 New Test Methods

1. **`test_configuration_parameters`** - Tests various VStore initialization parameters:
   - Custom `map_size`, `rebuild_threshold`, `max_workers`
   - `indexed_metadata_fields` functionality
   - Parameter validation and behavior

2. **`test_large_dataset_operations`** - Validates scalability with larger datasets:

body:
This pull request refactors the product management system to replace the use of `FormData` for handling product uploads with JSON-based requests and introduces direct image uploads to Cloudinary. These changes simplify the codebase, improve maintainability, and streamline image handling.

### API Refactor (Product Uploads)

* Removed `FormData` handling in `PUT` and `POST` endpoints for product updates and creation, replacing it with JSON-based body parsing. This eliminates the need for manual parsing and simplifies data handling. (`app/api/admin/products/[id]/route.ts` [app/api/admin/products/[id]/route.tsL21-L47](diffhunk://#diff-684facd78df53701bcafbc95328798d3714df8ef8c39afc6f210598bf1b87a6aL21-L47), `app/api/products/route.ts` [app/api/products/route.tsL78-L113](diffhunk://#diff-a2fd91299cc469f1146a3a5e426d802a20e73cb0e9820d140a9c4c22bf25169fL78-L113))
* Updated image handling logic to directly create database entries using Cloudinary URLs provided in the request body, removing the dependency on `uploadImagesToCloudinary`. (`app/api/admin/products/[id]/route.ts` [app/api/admin/products/[id]/route.tsL21-L47](diffhunk://#diff-684facd78df53701bcafbc95328798d3714df8ef8c39afc6f210598bf1b87a6aL21-L47), `app/api/products/route.ts` [app/api/products/route.tsL78-L113](diffhunk://#diff-a2fd91299cc469f1146a3a5e426d802a20e73cb0e9820d140a9c4c22bf25169fL78-L113))

### Frontend Updates (Product Management)

* Refactored `EditProductModal` and `NewProductForm` components to use JSON requests for product updates and creation, replacing `FormData` with direct Cloudinary URLs. (`components/admin/EditProductModal.tsx` [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-4961be0e79442ee3704ab775820b3b5932a9a9266af8503904c928a58fd48677L102-R142) `components/admin/NewProductForm.tsx` [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b6e9fd01957877a47ed1eefa83f607d51909fc63cffecefd0374852579b4c7a6L80-R113)
* Modified `ImageUploader` to handle direct uploads to Cloudinary, providing upload progress feedback and returning signed URLs for use in the application. (`components/admin/ImageUploader.tsx` [components/admin/ImageUploader.tsxR3-R56](diffhunk://#diff-421d6dd4645af3fcf496b44a425bbd575cece0e9497017d02928dc475a3178ecR3-R56))

### Code Cleanup and Removal

* Removed the `handleProductUpload` utility, including `parseProductFormData` and `uploadImagesToCloudinary`, as they are no longer required due to the shift to direct Cloudinary uploads. (`lib/handleProductUpload.ts` [lib/handleProductUpload.tsL1-L75](diffhunk://#diff-3be996602b3b1dc7c6cbdbd596c105d48512577093b407a6c55d0e03aa886a3cL1-L75))
* Added a new utility function `uploadToCloudinary` to encapsulate Cloudinary upload logic with progress tracking. (`lib/cloudinary/uploadToCloudinary.ts` [lib/cloudinary/uploadToCloudinary.tsR1-R28](diffhunk://#diff-15c386200639908c54ab09a21a9e5cd79d595a13a20ac349e880ed61a95c1b54R1-R28))Updates the API to accept JSON data instead of form data for product creation and updates.

Removes the dependency on manual form data parsing and Cloudinary uploading logic, streamlining the image upload process directly from the frontend.

Enhances error handling and improves the overall structure of the product management code.

Additionally, eliminates unused code and components related to previous file upload mechanisms.

author: marquescharlon
body:
Olá, boa tarde!

Imagino que este repositório seja para teste, portanto, utilizei para mostrar como faria um pull request.

Abaixo o passo a passo:

### Realizar o clone e as alterações
- Realizar o **fork**
- Realizar o clone para a máquina local. Ex.: `git clone link.git`
- Fazer as alterações necessárias
- Abrir o terminal (CMD) e executar o comando `git status` para verificar se à alteração está sendo observada
- Usar o `git add .` para adicionar à alteração 
- Usar o git commit para registrar esta alteração. Exe.: `git commit -m "Novo arquivo 'Charlon' adicionado"`
- Executar o `git push` para enviar o projeto da máquina local para o seu repositório no GitHub
- Dar `F5` (atualizar) o navegador e observar que as alterações já constam no repositório.

### Realizar o pull request
- Clicar no botão **Contribute**
- Clicar no botão **Open pull request**
- Escolher a `branch`, na qual, deseja enviar as alterações. 
- Por último, preencher os campos com as informações ou um breve resumo que colabore para o entendimento de quem irá analisar as alterações e aceitar o seu pull request.

author: edsu
body:
## Why was this change made? 🤔

We're seeing some errors in DSA during sdr-ingest-transfer in accessionWF when the `/dor/export` bag directory is being cleaned up using `Moab::Bagger.reset_bag()`:

https://app.honeybadger.io/projects/54415/faults/121047515/01JZJQF1PZS3WK8W7KQGB4HADY

From the stacktrace it appears that these are happening when the `data` directory doesn't exist? Since in both cases we are effectively doing a `rmtree` this change will simply do a `rmtree` instead of removing items in the directory and then the directory itself. The underlying filesystem is now WEKA NFS, and may not be behaving the way we expect it should.

It appears that DSA is the only code that is using `reset_bag()`?

https://github.com/search?q=org%3Asul-dlss+reset_bag&type=code&repo=&langOverride=&start_value=1

author: ovidiusm
body:
## What?
Bundles NIXL plugins into the packaged python wheel.

## Why?
So that the user can use NIXL plugins when installing nixl via `pip install nixl`.

## How?

The following changes were needed:

* copy NIXL plugins into the wheel, patching their RPATH
* patch the RPATH of all existing libs inside the wheel, so that they can load their dependencies correctly; this was not necessary before because there were no chains like python -> libnixl.so -> dlopen NIXL plugin -> direct-dep.so -> indirect-dep.so

Note that NIXL_PLUGIN_DIR must still be set to a directory inside the installed wheel, e.g. `venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/nixl.libs/nixl` This is probably not right, but it is a separate issue.

Tested with:

```
docker run -it --privileged --device=/dev/infiniband --net=host --ipc=host --gpus all -e NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all -e UCX_PROTO_INFO=y -v $PWD:/ws nvcr.io/nvidia/cuda-dl-base:25.03-cuda12.8-devel-ubuntu24.04 /bin/bash

apt update
apt install -y python3.12-venv
python3.12 -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate
pip install /ws/nixl-0.4.0-cp312-cp312-manylinux_2_28_x86_64.whl

python /ws/examples/python/nixl_api_example.py

export NIXL_PLUGIN_DIR=/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/nixl.libs/nixl

python /ws/nixl/examples/python/nixl_gds_example.py /tmp
```
